why: Cắt chuỗi theo [start, stop) có kiểm tra biên; chỉ strtol tràn khoảng int mới chạm chuyển đổi implementation-defined, đó là input bất thường.
Substring printing with bounds checks; start/stop compared against len after conversion to size_t, so valid input has defined behavior.
Substring printing with bounds checks against strlen; defined for valid integer arguments, UB only for pathological inputs (e.g. negative start, strtol out of int range).
Chủ đề là biến static cộng dồn; tràn số có dấu chỉ xảy ra khi stride rất lớn, không phải đường chạy chính.
Theme is a static running total; only possible signed overflow for huge strides is an ordinary error case.
Running sum in a static local; defined for ordinary strides, signed overflow only for extreme inputs.
pow kèm kiểm tra errno EDOM/ERANGE, hành vi xác định trên input hợp lệ.
Case is built around pow setting errno to EDOM/ERANGE, and whether math functions report errors via errno depends on implementation-defined math_errhandling.
Case is built around detecting pow() domain/range errors via errno, but whether pow sets errno depends on implementation-defined math_errhandling (glibc sets it, other libms may not).
Case Juliet CWE-121: hàm bad() ghi buffer[data] với data đọc từ stdin không kiểm cận trên, chủ đích kích hoạt ghi ngoài mảng.
Juliet-style bad() writes buffer[data] with an unchecked stdin index, so out-of-range input is an intended out-of-bounds write.
Juliet-style CWE-121 case: bad() writes buffer[data] with unchecked stdin index >= 10, an out-of-bounds store.

Named integer overflow: data+1 stored back into plain char, whose signedness and out-of-range conversion result are implementation-defined and are printed in hex.
Named integer_overflow: char data+1 stored back into char overflows for 0x7f/high bytes, giving implementation-defined conversion and output that depends on plain-char signedness.
